knowledge_gaps: The cosine residual is bounded, but SASRec logit scales may differ across categories and checkpoints. The proposed coefficient grid could therefore have negligible or inconsistent effects.

The diagnostic adapter does not explain how predict_score(features, items) obtains recent-history embeddings from features alone. Per-position residuals must use only the corresponding causal prefix, exclude padding, and match final-position inference.
Selecting coefficients on 200 validation users per category introduces selection optimism. Including zero preserves baseline eligibility but does not guarantee improved generalization.

Reproduction requires explicit checkpoint selection, normalization epsilon, empty-history handling, repeated-item weighting, and evaluator-equivalent candidate ordering and tie handling. The difficulty rating of 3 is optimistic until scoring parity is specified.

Recent embedding affinity may reinforce the broad similarity and redundancy already identified in feedback. A uniform-history affinity control and last-item-only control would help distinguish recency benefits from generic embedding smoothing.

follow_up_queries.reason: Determine whether score-scale mismatch makes the coefficient grid ineffective, and identify inexpensive controls that separate recency from generic similarity.
follow_up_queries.query: For sequential recommendation models combining SASRec dot-product logits with a recent-history cosine-similarity residual, what score calibration or fusion methods handle differing logit scales? What ablations compare exponentially weighted recent history, uniform history, and last-item-only similarity without pretrained weights?

follow_up_queries.reason: Resolve the missing causal adapter design and establish checks that diagnostic scores reproduce deployed inference.
follow_up_queries.query: How can a PyTorch SASRec scoring adapter expose per-position features containing both transformer states and a causal recent-item embedding average, while preserving log2feats(sequence) and predict_score(features, items)? Include left-padding masks, repeated items, zero-norm handling, and tests for final-position scoring parity and future-token leakage.

follow_up_queries.reason: Clarify how to interpret small validation gains after coefficient selection without changing the pinned benchmark or accessing test labels.
follow_up_queries.query: In recommender evaluation with 200 validation users per dataset and one positive plus 99 fixed negative candidates, how should researchers quantify uncertainty and selection optimism when choosing among four score-fusion coefficients per dataset? Discuss paired stratified user bootstrap intervals, validation reuse, and limitations of post-selection significance claims.
